feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for senior digital/public-sector roles: the positioning is clear, experience progression is logical, and the content shows real scope across platforms, governance, analytics, and multimedia. It reads professionally, but impact would improve with sharper outcomes, less repetition across skills sections, and a few style/grammar fixes.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear senior-level narrative with strong specialization in digital platform leadership, public-sector communications, and enterprise web modernization.  
- Good credibility signals: long tenure at NACo, internal progression, recognizable tools, and concrete scale indicators like “10,000+ page website” and “3.5 million annual page views.”  
- Writing is generally polished and strategic, with effective use of action verbs and a modern, relevant skills mix including AI-enabled search.

1. Top improvements  
- Add more measurable outcomes beyond scope metrics: e.g., traffic growth, engagement uplift, production efficiency, cost savings, adoption rates, or campaign results.  
- Reduce duplication between “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT”; consolidate to tighten structure and save space.  
- Fix style/grammar consistency: “social, and multimedia” should be “social and multimedia”; standardize serial comma usage; “A2/Learning” is awkward—use “A2 (learning)”; “Coleman DAVIS” capitalization may feel inconsistent unless intentional branding.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible intro with clear seniority and domain focus, but it reads slightly broad and repeats themes already covered in the subtitle, competencies, and experience. Tightening it around enterprise impact and public-sector relevance would make it sharper.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Replace “building the platforms” with stronger outcome-led phrasing such as “leading” or “modernizing” to emphasize senior ownership.
- Trim the long list of functions; group related areas to improve flow and avoid sounding like a skills dump.
- Consider a rewrite: “Senior digital leader with 12+ years of experience leading enterprise web modernization, governance, analytics, and content operations for high-volume public-sector communications. Builds scalable editorial and multimedia systems, strengthens digital infrastructure, and delivers AI-enabled user experiences for complex, mission-driven organizations.”
- Keep “public-sector” and “mission-driven organizations,” as they differentiate the profile well.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “AI-enabled user experiences” overlaps with Core Competencies and Recent Projects; keep it brief here.
- “Governance models/content operations” and “analytics infrastructure/editorial systems” are repeated elsewhere almost verbatim.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block overlaps heavily with the header, Topline Skills, and Technical sections. It would be stronger if tightened to emphasize leadership-level capabilities rather than repeating detailed skill categories.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Use broader, executive-level phrasing to reduce duplication: Enterprise web modernization • Digital governance and content operations • Analytics, reporting, and performance optimization • Cross-channel communications leadership • AI-enabled search and content discovery • Workflow automation and platform integration • Public-sector advocacy communications • Multimedia and livestream production
- Standardize style by replacing “&” with “and” for consistency across the CV.
- Consider changing “Multi-channel communications operations” to “Cross-channel communications leadership” to better reflect seniority.
- Consider shortening “AI-enabled search and content experiences” to “AI-enabled search and content discovery” for clarity.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section substantially repeats the header summary and Topline Skills; keep it high-level and avoid tool-specific or channel-specific detail.
- “Multimedia production and livestream operations” is also covered in Topline Skills and Work Experience, so avoid expanding it further here.
feedback.footer:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant project snapshot, but it reads like a repeat of the recent consulting and NACo experience rather than a distinct closing highlight section. Tightening phrasing and making formatting more scannable will improve impact.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Add a short lead-in such as “Selected Recent Projects” and format each item as a compact one-line project + outcome statement.
- Tighten wording: “AI-enabled” appears repeatedly; vary phrasing and remove filler like “designed for continued campaign growth.”
- Standardize style and punctuation: use parallel verb-led phrasing and spell out “10-by-20-foot” for consistency.
- Consider this rewrite: “Selected Recent Projects: AI Hybrid Search — Built a legislative search experience combining hybrid retrieval, structured content workflows, vector search, and bill-level AI chat. We Are Counties Microsite — Developed a Drupal 10 campaign microsite with custom navigation, interactive storytelling modules, and downloadable resources. Organization Anniversary Campaign — Produced a multi-part digital campaign featuring editorial storytelling, archival media, web features, and a 10-by-20-foot interactive conference display. Advocacy Video Series — Launched a recurring advocacy video program spanning planning, production, and distribution across web, email, and social.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- AI Hybrid Search, microsite work, and advocacy video series closely overlap with Work Experience bullets; keep this section shorter and more showcase-oriented to avoid repetition.

items.title: Coleman DAVIS
items.subtitle: Digital Platform & Communications Systems Leader
items.content: Senior digital leader with 12+ years of experience building the platforms, governance models and content operations behind high-volume public-sector communications. Leads enterprise web modernization, analytics infrastructure, editorial systems, multimedia production and AI-enabled user experiences for complex, mission-driven organizations.

items.title: Email
items.content: colemandavis4@gmail.com

items.title: Website
items.content: https://colemanpdavis.com/

items.title: Core Competencies
items.content: Enterprise website modernization • Digital governance & editorial systems • Analytics and reporting infrastructure • Multi-channel communications operations • AI-enabled search and content experiences • Workflow automation and platform integration • Advocacy and public-sector communications • Multimedia production and livestream operations

items.title: CV Footer
items.content:
### Recent Projects
**AI Hybrid Search**
Designed an AI-enabled legislative search experience combining hybrid retrieval, structured content workflows, vector search and bill-level AI chat to improve discovery of complex policy content.
**We Are Counties Microsite**
Built a Drupal 10 campaign microsite with custom navigation, interactive storytelling modules, downloadable resources and a modular structure designed for continued campaign growth.
**Organization Anniversary Campaign**
Developed a multi-part digital campaign combining editorial storytelling, archival media, web features and a 10×20-foot interactive conference display connected to the main site.
**Advocacy Video Series**
Built a recurring advocacy video program spanning editorial planning, production and distribution across website, email and social channels.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: Freelance (full-time engagement)
items.content:
Support a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with good scope and technical depth, but it reads as a task list. Tighten the language and foreground 2–3 concrete outcomes or flagship initiatives to make it feel more senior and distinct from the NACo entries.

Suggested edit:
- Open with impact, not support: “Lead digital strategy, platform improvement and content operations for a U.S. national membership organization.”
- Consolidate overlapping bullets into 4–5 sharper lines, e.g. combine systems/workflows/analytics and governance/usability/operations.
- Add measurable outcomes where possible: size of web estate, number of stakeholders/publishers, campaign launches, toolkit downloads, search accuracy/adoption, reduced publishing time, or performance gains.
- Suggested phrasing: “Built Drupal-based campaign microsites, modular storytelling components and member toolkits; improved enterprise workflows, analytics and governance across web, email, social and multimedia; led AI-enabled search strategy spanning retrieval design, structured content and user discovery.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Governance,” “analytics,” and “enterprise web improvement” closely overlap with the Director of Digital Media role—differentiate by emphasizing consulting ownership, AI search, and hands-on Drupal/build execution.
- Project details already appear in Recent Projects; avoid repeating the same examples verbatim.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-scope leadership entry with good scale metrics. It will be stronger if you tighten the opening, foreground the biggest transformation outcomes, and avoid repeating channel-management points covered in earlier NACo roles.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the opening with a sharper scope statement: “Directed NACo’s digital media function across web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget management.”
- Lead with the website transformation and outcome: “Spearheaded redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page Drupal website serving 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Make channel leadership more outcome-based; add growth, engagement, or production volume if available instead of “tens of thousands”/“thousands.”
- Tighten the remaining bullets to emphasize executive-level impact: built first in-house broadcast studio; expanded analytics stack (GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, BigQuery); formalized governance and publishing standards to improve cross-department planning.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the prior NACo role; keep this entry focused on scale, transformation, and systems leadership.
- Video-program growth also appears earlier; here, emphasize building the studio/capability, not recurring production.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps heavily with the later Director role and earlier Digital Media Manager role. Make it more clearly about operational leadership, editorial systems, and channel growth at the manager-to-director transition point.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite the lead to emphasize scope and progression: “Directed day-to-day digital communications operations across NACo’s web, email, social and video channels, scaling editorial coordination and advocacy messaging across teams.”
- Tighten bullets and foreground outcomes: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Make the video bullet more active and outcome-focused: “Launched and grew a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.”
- Combine planning/workflow bullets into one stronger line: “Built more consistent editorial planning and publishing workflows across communications, advocacy and program teams, improving coordination and execution.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Digital publishing workflows” and “editorial coordination” overlap with the Director role’s “governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.”
- Weekly video updates are also referenced in the 2015–2018 role; distinguish this entry as scaling/formalizing the program, not starting it.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong positioning, but this skills block overlaps heavily with the header and Core Competencies. It should be tighter and more distinctive, emphasizing leadership scope and strategic strengths not already repeated elsewhere.

Suggested edit:
- Replace generic phrases with sharper, executive-level wording:
- Enterprise digital strategy & governance
- Editorial operations and publishing standards
- Cross-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector advocacy and stakeholder messaging
- Audience strategy and content planning
- Consider reducing to 4 bullets for punchier scanning; “audience-focused content planning” and “public-sector and advocacy messaging” are the least differentiated.
- If you want more impact, swap one bullet for a stronger leadership signal, e.g. “Digital transformation for high-volume public-facing platforms.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy,” “editorial systems and governance,” and “multi-channel communications” substantially repeat the header and Core Competencies.
- “Public-sector and advocacy messaging” also echoes multiple NACo experience bullets; keep only if this audience specialization is a target-role priority.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill mix, but this item is too tool-heavy and overlaps heavily with the Technical + IT section. In Topline Skills, it should emphasize higher-value platform leadership and execution themes, not repeat every platform and language.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from a software list to a capability-led line, e.g.: “Drupal and enterprise CMS delivery • Website modernization and migration • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript) • API and workflow integrations • Airtable-based systems • AI-enabled search experiences”
- Drop lower-priority or older-feeling items here, especially “jQuery,” unless it is central to current target roles.
- Group overlapping CMS tools: “Drupal, WordPress, SharePoint and Power Pages” can become “Drupal and enterprise CMS platforms” if space is tight.
- If possible, align with recent impact: prioritize “CMS modernization,” “AI-enabled search,” and “workflow integrations” because they are reinforced by current/fresh experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item substantially duplicates “Technical + IT”; keep Topline Skills broader and save full tool inventory for that section.
- “AI-enabled search experiences” also appears in Core Competencies, so avoid overemphasizing it in both places unless it is a target-role differentiator.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster for recent leadership roles, but it overlaps heavily with “Core Competencies” and “Technical + IT.” Tighten it to emphasize decision-making impact, not just tool names.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe as outcomes-oriented: “GA4, BigQuery, Power BI, Looker Studio, Microsoft Clarity • KPI framework design • executive/leadership dashboards • SEO and digital performance analysis”
- Replace “Leadership reporting” with “Executive dashboards” or “Board/executive reporting” for sharper phrasing.
- Consider “Measurement strategy” instead of “KPI design” if you want a more senior, enterprise-level tone.
- If space allows, add one impact cue: “analytics infrastructure and reporting” to connect tools to business use.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates “Analytics and reporting infrastructure” in Core Competencies and “Data, Analytics & Optimization” in Technical + IT.
- Avoid listing the exact same tools in all three places; keep Topline Skills higher-level and leave full tool inventory to Technical + IT.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This skill block is relevant, but it’s generic and overlaps with both Core Competencies and multiple NACo bullets. Tighten it to emphasize higher-value, recent capabilities rather than listing basic production tasks.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe toward leadership and delivery scope, e.g. “Broadcast-quality video production • Livestream and hybrid event delivery • In-house studio operations • PTZ camera systems”
- Drop “video editing” unless paired with a stronger term like “end-to-end video production”; editing alone reads too tactical for your current level.
- Consider adding scale or context if format allows: “for advocacy, conferences, and recurring executive content”
- Keep to 4 items max and prioritize capabilities tied to the 2022–present roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Multimedia production and livestream operations” already appears in Core Competencies; use this section to add specificity, not repeat the same phrasing.
- “Hybrid and virtual event production” overlaps with “Livestreaming”; combine them into one stronger phrase.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it reads as a generic inventory and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution.” Since Drupal is the strongest and most recent platform in the CV, this item should emphasize depth/relevance or be trimmed.

Suggested edit:
- Reorder by relevance/recency: “Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages” is fine, but consider signaling strength: “Drupal (enterprise/public-sector) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages.”
- If space allows, add light qualifiers instead of just names: “Drupal site building/microsites • WordPress administration • SharePoint publishing • Power Pages • GitHub Pages.”
- Keep this item platform-focused only; avoid adding CMS modernization or technical execution terms already covered elsewhere.
- If you want more impact, replace GitHub Pages with a more substantive platform only if used meaningfully in recent work.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This duplicates the “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” topline skills section almost exactly.
- “Power Pages” may also feel redundant with broader Microsoft ecosystem tools listed elsewhere unless it played a real role.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical stack, but it reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution.” Make it more implementation-focused and trim older/basic items unless they support recent work.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe around applied capabilities, e.g.: “Front-end implementation: HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery”
- Group modern tooling by use case: “Integrations & deployment: API integrations, GitHub Actions, Cloudflare Workers”
- Keep only tools you actively use in recent roles; consider dropping “HTML5/CSS3” styling and use “HTML/CSS” for concision
- If possible, add evidence in adjacent experience bullets rather than here (e.g., GTM setup, serverless workflows, deployment automation, troubleshooting for Drupal properties)

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This duplicates “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” and “API integrations” already listed under Topline Skills
- “Google Tag Manager” may fit better under analytics/measurement rather than coding unless you specifically implemented tagging architecture

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is useful but currently reads as a generic tool dump. It should better distinguish true automation/build systems from general collaboration tools, especially since “workflow automation” and “Airtable systems” already appear elsewhere.

Suggested edit:
- Split into two clearer categories or narrow the title. Example: “Automation & Workflow Tools: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana” and move Slack, Teams, Basecamp, Trello to a separate “Collaboration & Project Tools” line.
- Prioritize strongest, most relevant tools first: Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier, Jira, Asana.
- If space allows, add light qualifiers to show depth, e.g. “Airtable (workflow databases), Power Automate (Microsoft ecosystem), Zapier (cross-platform automation).”
- Consider renaming to “Workflow Automation & Project Systems” if keeping Jira/Asana here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Airtable systems” and “Workflow automation” already appear in Topline Skills, so avoid repeating the same phrasing verbatim.
- Slack and Teams are more collaboration platforms than automation systems; keeping them here weakens the category.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too bare to add much value. Since email leadership already appears strongly in recent NACo roles, this line should emphasize platform depth and audience-engagement systems rather than repeat “email” generally.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Email Marketing & Engagement Platforms
- Rewrite as: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
- If accurate, strengthen with qualifiers: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys (campaign automation, segmentation, journeys) • Higher Logic (member communications/community engagement) • Mailchimp
- Keep platform names only here; save strategy, newsletter scale, and channel leadership for recent work experience bullets.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Email” is already prominent in multiple recent NACo entries, so avoid adding generic phrases like “email marketing” or “newsletter management” elsewhere in this section.
- Higher Logic may overlap with membership/community functions; only add that descriptor if it reflects actual hands-on use.

items.title: Data, Analytics & Optimization
items.content: GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • Looker Studio • Power BI • BigQuery • SEO • A/B testing • Dashboarding
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tool stack, but this item largely duplicates “Topline Skills > Analytics, Insights & Optimization” and reads as a keyword list rather than a differentiated technical category. Tighten it and emphasize methods/tools not already covered elsewhere.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Data & Optimization Tools
- Replace with: GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • BigQuery • Power BI • Looker Studio • Google Search Console • A/B testing
- Drop “Dashboarding” since it’s implied by Power BI/Looker Studio; add “Google Search Console” if SEO is a meaningful hands-on tool area.
- If space allows, use grouped phrasing for clarity: Analytics: GA4, Clarity, BigQuery • Reporting: Power BI, Looker Studio • Optimization: A/B testing, SEO

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This is near-duplicate of “Topline Skills > Analytics, Insights & Optimization”; consider keeping strategy items there and reserving this section for tools only.
- “SEO” also overlaps with broader performance analysis language elsewhere; keep only if it reflects direct execution.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal, but the item is still broad and reads like setup for later NACo roles. Tighten it around foundational impact, team-building, and specific outputs without repeating responsibilities already covered in 2018–2024 entries.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to emphasize progression + first-team build: “Promoted across two digital roles to help establish NACo’s first in-house digital team and formalize workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia.”
- Add clearer outcomes if available: website traffic, livestream/event volume, video cadence, email growth, turnaround time, or production cost/time saved.
- Make contributions more concrete: “Supported a major website refresh, produced livestreams and weekly video updates, and coordinated day-to-day content production.”
- Replace “providing day-to-day guidance” with stronger management phrasing if accurate: “mentored” or “supervised” a digital media associate.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 role; keep this item focused on launching/building the format rather than expanding it.
- Avoid repeating broad workflow language already used in later NACo entries unless you can show this role introduced the initial systems.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry that shows initiative, especially the first podcast launch. It should be tightened and framed around outcomes or “firsts,” while avoiding overlap with later digital/media roles.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to emphasize initiative and scope: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives supporting NACo programs and policy priorities.”
- Make the podcast achievement the lead proof point: “Launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, scripting, guest/stakeholder coordination, and production.”
- Compress the rest into one supporting clause: “Produced digital and multimedia content to support program communications and policy storytelling.”
- If possible, add one measurable detail: number of episodes, audience, internal stakeholders supported, or types of projects delivered.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Digital content production and multimedia materials” overlaps with later digital/media roles; keep this higher-level and avoid repeating video/livestream language used in 2015–2024 entries.
- “Supporting organizational programs and policy work” is vague; specify functions only if they add distinct context not covered elsewhere.

items.title: Multimedia & Creative Tools
items.content: Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • Livestream studio workflows • Podcast production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is relevant, but it reads as a mixed list of software and capabilities. It also overlaps with “Multimedia Production & Event Delivery” and several work bullets, so it should be tightened to emphasize tools only.

Suggested edit:
- Split tools from production capabilities; keep this line software-focused.
